Name: Cheesemakers Guild - An Animal Product and Rancher Profession Expansion
Author: HarrisonGrey
Description:
[center]Want something more to do with your animal products? Looking for added incentives to going for the Coopmaster or Shepherd professions? Then the [b]Cheesemakers Guild[/b] mod is for you![/center]
[b]Join the Gem Sea Cheesemakers Guild[/b]
﻿This mod aims to add depth to animal produce through a couple new features. First and foremost is the new Gem Sea[b] Cheesemakers Guild Apprenticeship[/b], which you can access through a pamphlet found occasionally among the Bookseller's wares once you've reached Farming level 10. Reading the pamphlet will send you a checklist in the mail of the 8 new cheeses you can make. These cheeses are:
[list]
[*][b]Paneer[/b]: a fresh cheese used for cooking.
[i]312g[/i][/*]
[*]﻿[b]Brie[/b]: A soft cheese, pairs well with berries.
[i]625g[/i][/*]
[*]﻿[b]Mozzarella[/b]: A stretchy cheese that can be aged for further flavor.
[i]312g[/i]  ﻿[/*]
[*][b][b]Blue Cheese[/b]:[/b] A pungent cheese that develops blue veins as it ages.[i] [/i]
[i]450g[/i][/*]
[*][b]Feta[/b]: A flavorful brined cheese.
[i]510g[/i][/*]
[*][b]Añejo[/b]: A high quality, hard cheese made from Goat Milk.
[i]1380g[/i][/*]
[*][b]Beaufort[/b]: A high quality, hard cheese made from Cow Milk.
[i]1140g[/i][/*]
[/list]           
And, if you have [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/22256]Selph's Extra Machine Configs[/url], you can also make:
[list]
[*][b]Truffle Cheese[/b]: A hard cheese with truffles mixed in.
[i]1875g[/i][/*]
[/list]
﻿Some of the new cheeses require cow milk while others require goat; a few can be made using either. These cheeses do receive a price boost if made using goat milk. Most of these can be made using small or large milk; cheeses made with large milk will produce Gold quality cheese.
﻿How do you make these cheeses? That's part of the game! There are no new machines or items needed to make these cheeses, but the exact conditions that make them you'll have to figure out yourself. You will have help; [b]someone in town[/b] is already a qualified member of the Cheesemakers Guild and can give you hints as to how to make each cheese. Also, the [b]checklist[/b] you receive doesn't just tell you what cheeses are now available, but it updates with specific instructions once you've successfully made each cheese, that way you'll always have your cheesemaking notes to consult.

﻿In addition to these new cheeses, the Apprenticeship also unlocks [b]Pickled Eggs[/b] which can be made by placing 3 small eggs (Chicken or Duck) or 1 large egg (Ostrich or Dinosaur) in a Preserves Jar. The pickled eggs take 4000 minutes and boost prices by about 4-5 times, depending on the egg type.
[b]Note for Modders[/b]: The Pickled Eggs recipe can automatically use any custom eggs added by mods as long as the egg has the -5 (egg) category or contains the context tag "category_egg"; this will require a stack of 3 eggs. If you'd like your egg to require only 1 per stack, give it the context tag "giant_egg_item". I've added the "giant_egg_item" context tag to a couple modded eggs, like Mizu's Emu and the Dino Expanded eggs.
﻿The new items will not show up in your Shipping Collection until you've begun your Cheesemakers Guild Apprenticeship, meaning you can add this mod to your collection even late into a save and not have to worry about postponing a complete shipping collection by several more items. Additionally, reading the book a second time lets you cancel your guild membership, which removes all the items from your Shipping Collection and prevents machines from producing them until you restart your apprenticeship. Your notes and any items you still have in storage remain, and if you restart your apprenticeship the game will remember the count of how many of each you've shipped.

[b]More Cooking with Animal Produce[/b]
﻿Don't these new cheeses make you hungry? This mod adds 5 new recipes to highlight animal products:

[b]Paneer Tikka Masala[/b]
﻿Made with: Paneer, Tomato, and Rice
[b]Charchuterie Board[/b]
﻿Made with: Brie, Strawberry, and Hazelnuts
[b]Tuna Melt[/b]
﻿Made with: Tuna, Mozzarella, and Bread
[b]Eggs Benedict[/b]
﻿Made with: any Egg, Fried Egg, and Bread
[b]Truffle Fettuccine[/b]
﻿Made with: Wheat Flour, Cream, Truffle, and Garlic

These recipes (and cheeses) are [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/38862]Flexible Cooking[/url] friendly.
These recipes will be automatically sent to you in letters as you make new cheeses. As a backup, you can also configure these recipes to be purchasable at the Saloon once you've unlocked the new cheeses.

[b]Bonus Benefits to the Rancher Profession[/b]
﻿The Rancher Profession now comes with a number of benefits made to give it an edge over the vanilla Artisan profession. For starters, the most expensive new cheeses, Beaufort and Añejo, are produced more frequently when you have the Rancher profession.
﻿Cows and Goats can produce a new, rare deluxe produce item, [b]Cream[/b]. Cream can be turned into cheese, by default producing Iridium quality Cheese (with the possibility to produce up to 2 cheeses, depending on the quality of the Cream) though it can, under the right circumstances, also make some of the other, higher priced cheeses.
﻿All new cheeses and pickled eggs gain the 20% boost from the Rancher profession. This price boost is applied when the item is made, so cheeses made before the profession is changed will maintain their original price.
﻿The new recipes also gain buffs only when the player has the Rancher profession. Paneer Tikka Masala boosts speed and critical hit chance; Eggs Benedict boosts farming, foraging, and max stamina; the Tuna Melt makes all fish easier to catch within the next hour; and the Truffle Fettuccine grants the Oil of Garlic boost, blocking monsters from appearing. The Charcuterie Board becomes a Universally Loved gift.

[b]Compatibilities[/b]
[url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/1063]Automate[/url] - Parts of this mod respond to stats incremented when you harvest the new cheeses from the cheese  press; Automate interrupts this process and prevents that stat from being incremented. This stat only needs to be incremented once per cheese for you to receive the effects, so if you are using Automate and have not, for instance, received the new recipes in the mail, try manually harvesting each cheese once and once you've unlocked the recipes and filled out your cheese checklist, you can go back to using Automate.
[url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/38862]Flexible Cooking[/url] - As mentioned above, all new cheeses have Flexible Cooking context tags, either cheese_item or soft_cheese_item, allowing them to be used as a replacement for Cheese or Goat Cheese (respectively) in different recipes across [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/6830]Love of Cooking[/url] and [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/39057]Cornucopia[/url]. Paneer, the cooking cheese, counts as both and can replace any cheese in any recipe with flexible cooking options. If you do not have Flexible Cooking, this mod's recipes default to specific cheeses and ingredients.
[url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/1348]SpaceCore[/url] - Optional. SpaceCore is required for the flexible cooking option, but the mod can run without it.
[url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/41502]Exotic Cattle[/url] - The Cream added by this mod is the same item added by Exotic Cattle; Cream was a crucial item for both mods, so both add it on their own. If you have either of the mods but not the other, Cream will still be added as an item. If you have both mods, Exotic Cattle adds it and this mod doesn't. If you have both and remove one, the other mod will then add it so you won't see saved copies of the item disappear.
[url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/24842]Cornucopia[/url] - In addition to compatibility with Cornucopia's flexible recipes option, this mod turns off the Pickled Eggs if you have Cornucopia installed so as to use Cornucopia's Pickled Eggs instead; the config option Always Enable Pickled Eggs allows you to add this mod's Pickled Eggs even when you have Cornucopia, just in case you'd prefer the pricing mechanism of this mod's eggs. In this instance, adding a stack of eggs to the Preserves Jar makes my pickled eggs, while adding a single egg at a time makes Cornucopia's pickled eggs.
Cream can also be used in Cornucopia's Butter Churn to make Iridium quality Butter; the higher the quality of the Cream, the higher chance it produces 2 butter.
[url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/22256]Extra Machine Configs[/url] - Optional. EMC is required to make the Truffle Cheese in this mod. This mod can otherwise still run without EMC, the Truffle Cheese simply will not be added.
[url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/27321]Goat Mod[/url] - Female goats that produce milk added by this mod can occasionally produce Cream instead if you've got the Rancher profession.
[url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/42862]Cheesemonger[/url] - There shouldn't be any incompatibilities with Cheesemonger, though both mods will add their own versions of some of the same cheeses. The approach to cheese making is quite different between the two mods; Cheesemonger represents the process by adding new machines to separate milk curds from whey and to generate bacteria needed to make specific cheeses; this mod represents the process through the simplified interpretation of the vanilla game but with unique conditions resulting in different cheeses. Pick which version you'd like to use (or both, nothing's stopping you).
Seriously, I was 2 weeks into working on this mod and had the basics implemented when Cheesemonger posted and I couldn't believe it. That was even the original name of this mod, which you can probably tell if you look into some of the file names here.
